reason: The moving-wall condition u|∂Ω=g is ill-typed: g is never defined, including its domain, codomain, time dependence, or regularity. The definition standard requires these data to be explicit.

The boundary-condition clauses use u and g without defining their types or domains, so the trace equality is not fully specified. Define u as a vector field on a stated channel and g as data on the two wall faces.

F1 misstates the dependency: it calls the periodic x and z coordinates “streamwise,” but for the stated x-directed shear, z is transverse. The interface only says the first and third quotient coordinates are periodic.

Only u∈C²(I×Ω) on an open Lipschitz domain is assumed, which does not guarantee a boundary trace. Thus the selected no-slip datum u=0 on the wall is not operationally defined; the cited boundary-data interface requires continuous traces wherever data are imposed.

The imported forced-model fields have type I×Ω (time first), but the theorem declares b_phys on Ω×I and evaluates u_phys, p_phys, and b_phys at (x,t). This makes the scaling and step 1.1 ill-typed against the supplied model interface.
